title: Deep histogram tests: dispersion index, depth scan, and an exact finite-population theory of bin counts
summary: I rewrote the course histogram program (rnd_test_claude.f, fixed form, USE RNGLIB) as a general deep-histogram driver. It runs any generator in either precision for any number of bins B and draws N. Instead of a per-bin dump it reports compact summaries: empty bins, the dispersion index D = s^2/mean, the chi-square z-score, 4-sigma outliers against exact binomial expectations, and the count-of-counts table. I scanned depths B = 10^1 to 10^8 (100 hits per bin, 10 at B = 10^8) for all nine generators in double precision, for five generators stored in REAL*4, and for the even seed 65536. The good generators (MT19937, RANNUM, R250 in double) stayed within 2.3 sigma of the ideal at every depth. Every other generator failed at a depth that can be predicted exactly. The prediction comes from one rule: a generator that visits each reachable value once per period P gives, after N = qP + r draws, bin counts $n_b = q c_b + \mathrm{Hyp}(P, c_b, r)$, where $c_b$ is the measured one-period population of bin b. For floating-point storage, the bin probabilities come from the REAL*4 rounding cells. This rule, together with a rho-shaped model of the logistic map (which I found is periodic in double precision, cycle length 5,638,349), predicts all 112 non-logistic depth-scan values of D within 1.95 sigma. It also explains the student's observations: RANDU's too-even bins at 1e7 bins (D = 0.0710 measured vs 0.0711 predicted), RAND's empty bins and the bump at 238.4 (Binomial(512, 0.4657)), and the REAL*4 steps at 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 (block D = 8.76, 3.03, 1.46 matching the rounding model). Repeating the student's own 1e5-bin, 1e7-draw test over 200 seeds shows that RANDU and RANDM already fail it at about 4 sigma (mean z = -3.94 and -4.21; predicted -4.17) because the chi-square comes out too small. A one-sided reading of the chi-square detects this. The 4-sigma outlier count used by the course program does not.

methods.name: Deep-histogram driver (rnd_test_claude.f)
methods.description: Each job line (IGEN IPREC NBINS NDRAW ISEED ICOC NREG TAG) seeds one rnglib generator, sets rng_single=(IPREC==4), draws N numbers x and increments bin int(x*B)+1 (clamped to [1,B]). With $\lambda = N/B$ it reports: NEMPTY; sample variance $s^2=\sum_b(n_b-\lambda)^2/(B-1)$; dispersion index $D=s^2/\lambda$; Pearson $\chi^2=\sum_b (n_b-\lambda)^2/\lambda=(B-1)D$; and $z=(\chi^2-(B-1))/\sqrt{2(B-1)(1-1/N)}$. These are the exact multinomial mean and variance of $\chi^2$, so under the null $E[D]=1$ and $\mathrm{sd}(D)=\sqrt{2(1-1/N)/(B-1)}$. It also reports N4LO/N4HI, the number of bins with $(n_b-\lambda)/\sqrt{\lambda}\le -4$ or $\ge 4$ (the course criterion), and their exact expectations $B\,P(\mathrm{Bin}(N,1/B)\ \text{in tail})$ from log-gamma pmf sums. Optional outputs: the count-of-counts table (number of bins with exactly k hits) and a profile (mean and D in NREG consecutive blocks of bins, to locate an anomaly in x). Bins are integer*4; outputs are appended, one block per job.
methods.parameters: CL = 4; count-of-counts tabulated over [min,max] when the range is below 2e6, otherwise 0..2e6 plus an overflow line; compiled with gfortran 16 -O2 against a private copy of rnglib.o

methods.name: Depth scan
methods.description: $B=10^d$ for d=1..7 with N=100B ($\lambda=100$), and d=8 with N=1e9 ($\lambda=10$, limited by memory and time). Series: all 9 generators in double precision with seed 777; RANDU, MINSTD, MT19937, R250, RANNUM stored in REAL*4 (rng_single); RANDU and RANDM with seed 65536. Profiles with 1000 blocks for d>=6.
methods.parameters: 14 series x 8 depths = 112 runs plus 16 seed-65536 runs; 2.1e9 draws per series; about 13 CPU minutes on a heavily loaded machine

methods.name: Full-period population and finite-population (hypergeometric) theory
methods.description:
hist_period.f90 bins exactly one period of a generator into B=10^1..10^8 at once, with the driver's arithmetic. This gives $c_b$, the number of reachable outputs in bin b. It also checks the period: the integer state returns to the seed after exactly P steps and never before, and the next 16 outputs repeat the first 16. For N = qP + r draws the counts are modeled as $n_b = q c_b + h_b$ with $h_b \sim \mathrm{Hypergeometric}(P, c_b, r)$, i.e. the partial period acts as a random subset. Then $E[\sum_b (n_b-\lambda)^2]=\sum_b [\mathrm{Var}(h_b)+(c_b N/P-\lambda)^2]$, giving $E[D]$, and $\mathrm{sd}(D)$ uses a Gaussian approximation per bin. For $c_b \ll P$ this reduces to $D \approx (N/P)D_c + f(1-f)P/N$ with $f=r/P$ and $D_c=\mathrm{Var}(c_b)/\bar c$. For N

=1. The predicted count-of-counts is the mixture $\sum_b P(q c_b+\mathrm{Bin}(c_b,f)=k)/B$.
methods.parameters: RANDU and RANDM, seed 777: P = 2^29 = 536,870,912 (orbit = odd states congruent to 1 or 3 mod 8, the same set for both multipliers); seed 65536: P = 8192; MINSTD: P = 2^31-2; RAND: P = 2^31-2 with 2^22 values carrying 512 states each (the top value 510); REAL*4 versions of RANDU and MINSTD enumerated exactly

methods.name: REAL*4 rounding-cell model
methods.description: float_weights.f90 streams over every REAL*4 value f in [2^-40, 1) in increasing order. Each f gets the weight of its round-to-nearest cell [(f_prev+f)/2, (f+f_next)/2). The top float below 1 also gets [1-2^-25,1), because rnglib maps 1.0 back to it. The weights are summed into the bin containing f, giving exact bin probabilities $p_b$ for a continuous uniform input stored in REAL*4. With $w_b = B p_b$: $E[D]=1+(\lambda-1/B)\sum_b (w_b-1)^2/(B-1)$, and the count-of-counts is a Poisson($\lambda w_b$) mixture. Analytic octave form: in $[2^{-k-1},2^{-k})$ the float spacing is $u=2^{-k-24}$, each bin holds $\lfloor g\rfloor$ or $\lceil g\rceil$ floats with $g = 1/(Bu)$, and the block dispersion is $1+\lambda\,\mathrm{frac}(g)(1-\mathrm{frac}(g))/g^2$.
methods.parameters: applied to MT19937, RANNUM (53-bit inputs) and R250 (32-bit inputs, approximate) in REAL*4; for the double-precision word lattices k/2^32 (R250) and k/2^53 the analogous lattice weights are used

methods.name: Logistic-map cycle detection and rho model
methods.description: logis_cycle.f90 is a bit-exact replica of G_LOGIS (verified against rng_next for 1e7 draws, 0 mismatches). It applies Brent's algorithm to the double-precision state to find the tail length $\mu$ and cycle length L. Rho model of the histogram: tail points are visited once and cycle points (N-$\mu$)/L times, both placed in bins as independent Poisson samples. This gives $D=[\mu+L f(1-f)+(N-\mu)^2/L]/N$ with $f=\mathrm{frac}((N-\mu)/L)$, an empty fraction $e^{-(\mu+L)/B}$, and a comb-shaped count-of-counts.
methods.parameters: seed 777 plus a survey of 30 random seeds

methods.name: Student configuration repeated over seeds
methods.description: The student's histogram test (B=1e5, N=1e7, double precision) was run for 200 odd seeds drawn from numpy default_rng(777) for RANDU, RANDM, RAND, MINSTD, R250, RANNUM and MT19937. The z distributions were compared with the theory prediction $N(\mu_z,\sigma_z)$ (t-test on the mean, KS test).

methods.name: Serial-correlation check on the null distribution
methods.description: 1000 random seeds of LOGISTIC, MT19937 and RANNUM at B=100, N=1e4 (well inside the logistic transient). Statistics: KS test of $\chi^2$ against $\chi^2_{99}$, SD of z, fraction with |z|>3. A second run wrote per-bin counts (profile with NREG=B) to estimate the per-bin variance ratio $\phi_b=\mathrm{Var}(n_b)/\lambda$ across seeds.

methods.name: RAND identity check
methods.description: rand_check.f90 runs G_RAND and G_MINSTD from the same seed side by side for 2e8 draws. It compares RAND with $\lfloor (s-1)/2^9\rfloor\,2^{-22}$ and with $\lfloor 2^{22}s/(2^{31}-1)\rfloor\,2^{-22}$, where s is the MINSTD state, then builds RAND's exact one-period table from the verified identity.

findings.claim: The deep histogram cleanly separates the generators. MT19937, RANNUM and R250 (double) stay within the null at every depth up to B=1e8. Every other generator fails beyond a characteristic depth, either too even (D<1) or too uneven (D>1).
findings.evidence: Validation on good generators (24 runs, B=10 to 1e8): max |z| = 2.31 (R250 at B=1e8). At B=1e7, N=1e9 the 4-sigma outliers were MT 112 low and 892 high, R250 106 and 911, RANNUM 104 and 878, against exact binomial expectations of 108.1 and 916.5. Empty bins at B=1e8 (lambda=10): 4526, 4528, 4550 vs Poisson 4540 +/- 67. Failures at B=1e7, N=1e9: RANDU D=0.0710 (z=-2077), RANDM 0.0710, MINSTD 0.535 (z=-1040), RAND 139 (z=3.1e5), LOGISTIC 172 (z=3.8e5), MIDSQ 1e9. At B=1e8: RANDU 0.190, MINSTD 0.540, RAND 229, LOGISTIC 172.

findings.claim: RANDU and RANDM bins are too even because the generator has run through its whole period. A finite-population (hypergeometric) model built from the exact one-period histogram predicts D at every depth. RANDU and RANDM visit exactly the same 2^29 states (odd states congruent to 1 or 3 mod 8) in different orders, so their predictions coincide.
findings.evidence: Period verified as exactly 2^29 for both (state returns after 536,870,912 steps and never before). B=1e7, N=1e9 (q=1, f=0.8626): predicted D=0.071072 +/- 0.000032, measured RANDU 0.071020 (-1.65 sd) and RANDM 0.071045 (-0.86 sd). Bin counts ran from 84 to 108, against Poisson(100) bulk of about 60 to 140. B=1e6, N=1e8: predicted 0.813903 +/- 0.00115, measured 0.813871 and 0.812966. B=1e8, N=1e9: predicted 0.189920 +/- 0.00002, measured 0.189914 and 0.189924. RANDU at B=1e7 had zero 4-sigma outliers where 1024.6 are expected for a perfect generator (Poisson probability about e^-1025).

findings.claim: MINSTD, with N=1e9 about half its period, shows D close to 1-N/P = 0.534 as predicted. The deficit also appears in the empty-bin count at B=1e8, where sampling without replacement leaves 30 times fewer empty bins than Poisson.
findings.evidence: P = 2^31-2 verified. B=1e7, N=1e9: predicted D = 0.534747 +/- 0.000239, measured 0.534823 (+0.32 sd); counts 57 to 138. B=1e6, N=1e8: predicted 0.953439 +/- 0.00135, measured 0.954224 (z_null = -32.4). B=1e8, N=1e9: 146 empty bins against Poisson 4540 +/- 67 (65 sigma) and a model prediction of 149.8 = 1e8(1-f)^{21.47}.

findings.claim: RAND's bimodal count-of-counts follows exactly from the identity RAND = floor((s-1)/2^9) 2^-22. Every one of its 2^22 values carries 512 MINSTD states, so at B=1e7 a bin holds 0 or 512 states. That gives a spike at 0 (58.06 percent of bins) and a Binomial(512, N/P) bump near 238.
findings.evidence: Identity: 0 mismatches in 2e8 draws (the alternative floor(2^22 s/M) 2^-22 mismatched 390,584 times). B=1e7, N=1e9: empty bins = 5,805,696 = 1e7 - 2^22 exactly. Filled-bin mean 238.42 and SD 11.284, against Binomial(512, 0.465661) mean 238.42 and SD 11.287. Predicted D 138.953 +/- 0.006, measured 138.953. B=1e8: 95,805,696 empty bins = 1e8 - 2^22, D 228.953 (predicted 228.953). B=1e6: D=1.846 vs 1.843 +/- 0.0024, first failing at z=598. At the student's B=1e5 the prediction is only -0.36 sigma, so RAND passes there.

findings.claim: The student's own 1e5-bin, 1e7-draw test already detects RANDU's and RANDM's finite period at about 4 sigma in almost every run. The chi-square is too small, and the 4-sigma outlier count is blind to this. In general a period-P generator fails the lambda=100 histogram test at 3 sigma once $N \gtrsim 12 P^{2/3}$, because $z \approx -(N/P)\sqrt{(B-1)/2}$.
findings.evidence: Predicted z = -4.17 (D = 0.98137 +/- 0.00439). Over 200 odd seeds: RANDU mean z = -3.94 (sd 1.22) and RANDM -4.21 (sd 0.86). z < -3 in 74 percent and 91 percent of runs, z < -1.96 in 93.5 and 99 percent; the highest RANDU z was -1.18. Seed 777: z = -4.41. Null controls: R250 +0.04 (KS p=0.57), RANNUM +0.08 (p=0.39), MT19937 -0.03 (p=0.81). MINSTD -0.83 (predicted -1.04), RAND -0.15 (predicted -0.36). The scaling law gives N* about 8e6 for RANDU (B about 8e4) and 2e7 for MINSTD (B about 2e5), consistent with failures first appearing at d=5 and d=6.

findings.claim: The even seed 65536 reduces RANDU and RANDM to the same 8192 values (u/2^15 with u congruent to 1 or 3 mod 8). D swings from far too even at shallow depth to enormously too uneven, and the histogram becomes deterministic. Prime-modulus MINSTD has no such seed sensitivity.
findings.evidence: P = 8192 verified for both. Measured D vs prediction: B=100: 0.137 vs 0.142 +/- 0.020; B=1e3: 0.241 vs 0.245; B=1e4: 69.761 vs 69.762, with 3408 of 1e4 bins empty (exactly predicted); B=1e5: 1120.71; B=1e7: 121,970 with 9,991,808 empty bins and every filled bin holding 122,070 or 122,071 hits (q=122,070, f=0.3125), as the student found.

findings.claim: Storing any generator in REAL*4 makes the histogram too uneven at B >= 1e6. This is a floating-point artifact that depends only on the octave of x. An exact rounding-cell model reproduces D at every depth and the steps the student saw at 1/2, 1/4, 1/8.
findings.evidence: Model D for continuous input at lambda=100: 1.00037 (B=1e5, invisible: 0.08 sigma), 1.0366 (B=1e6), 5.4548 (B=1e7), 31.454 (B=1e8, lambda=10). MT19937 REAL*4 measured 1.0373 (z_null=26.4), 5.4535 (-0.99 sd), 31.456; RANNUM 1.0345, 5.4543, 31.457; R250 1.0378, 5.4546, 31.455. Block D at B=1e7 matches $1+\lambda\,\mathrm{frac}(g)(1-\mathrm{frac}(g))/g^2$: model 8.760/3.035/1.456/1.135 vs MT 8.760/3.033/1.455/1.137 in [1/2,1), [1/4,1/2), [1/8,1/4), [1/16,1/8). At B=1e8, 62,334,176 bins (62.33 percent) contain no REAL*4 value at all; every REAL*4 series showed 62.33 to 62.34 percent empty bins. RANDU and MINSTD in REAL*4 combine both effects: D = 4.5185 (pred 4.5185 +/- 0.0003) and 4.9884 (pred 4.9891 +/- 0.0009), i.e. the MT value minus their period deficits of 0.93 and 0.47.

findings.claim: The double-precision logistic map (the chaotic negative control) is secretly periodic. From seed 777 it enters a cycle of 5,638,349 states after 14,324,259 steps, and a rho-shaped model predicts its histogram (D, empty fraction, comb-shaped count-of-counts) at every depth.
findings.evidence: Brent cycle detection on a bit-exact replica. Model vs measured: D at N=1e8 (B=1e6) 13.171 +/- 0.019 vs 13.166; N=1e9 (B=1e7) 172.327 +/- 0.106 vs 172.363; B=1e8 172.327 vs 172.343. Empty fraction at B=1e7: 0.135842 vs 0.135798; at B=1e8: 0.819037 vs 0.818994. The count-of-counts at B=1e7 forms a comb at multiples of 174 to 175 cycle visits. Survey of 30 random seeds: 21 enter the same 5,638,349 cycle, 6 collapse to the fixed point 0 (through 1/2 -> 1 -> 0 in rounding), and 3 enter cycles of 14,632,801, 2,625,633 and 2,441,806 states; tails range from 1.37e6 to 8.0e7.

findings.claim: Test property: for a serially correlated sequence with an exactly uniform marginal (the tent-map conjugate of the logistic map), D keeps mean 1, but its sampling distribution is much wider than the chi-square null. So isolated 4-sigma excursions at shallow depth are expected and do not by themselves indicate a bad marginal.
findings.evidence: LOGISTIC at B=100, N=1e4, 1000 seeds: mean D = 0.988, SD 0.243 vs null 0.142 (variance ratio 2.93), |z|>3 in 6.2 percent of runs vs 0.27 percent, KS against chi2(99) p = 6e-28. MT19937: SD 0.139, KS p = 0.19. RANNUM: SD 0.144, p = 0.69. Per-bin variance ratio is highest in the bins holding the tent-map fixed points: phi = 2.75 for [0,0.01) and 2.59 for [0.66,0.67) (x=2/3), mean phi = 0.978. The seed-777 depth-scan value at B=100 (D=1.618, z=4.35) is the only one of 120 points outside 2 sigma of its prediction; against the empirical LOGISTIC spread it is 2.6 sd.

findings.claim: Overall validation: the finite-population and rounding theory, with no free parameters, reproduces all measured dispersion indices. That makes the histogram test quantitatively understood: every deviation is either period exhaustion, a missing-values lattice, or REAL*4 rounding.
findings.evidence: 112 non-logistic depth-scan points: max |measured - predicted|/sd = 1.95, rms 0.84 (several series share sequences, so the points are not independent). Including LOGISTIC, 119 of 120 points are within 2 sd; the exception is H9.

findings.claim: Control: MIDSQ with the default seed 777 is a constant generator. It reaches the absorbing state 0 at the second draw, so the histogram puts all draws but one into the first bin and D = N exactly.
findings.evidence: 777^2/10^4 = 60, then 60^2/10^4 = 0. At B=1e7, N=1e9: 9,999,998 empty bins, one bin with 999,999,999 hits, D = 1.0e9. D = N at every depth (1000 at B=10).

figures.caption: Depth scan with 100 expected hits per bin ($\lambda=10$ at $B=10^8$), seed 777, double precision. Left: dispersion index D. Middle: chi-square z-score (symmetric log axis). Right: fraction of empty bins. The gray bands are the ideal $\pm3\sigma$ ranges. MT19937, RANNUM and R250 stay at D = 1 at every depth. RANDU and RANDM (identical curves) and MINSTD drop below 1 once the draws approach their periods, while RAND, LOGISTIC and MIDSQ blow up.

Count-of-counts (fraction of bins receiving exactly k hits) at $B=10^7$, $N=10^9$ for all nine generators, against the ideal Poisson(100) (dashed) and the finite-period model (solid). RANDU and RANDM are far narrower than Poisson, MINSTD is a Binomial with half the Poisson variance, and RAND splits into a spike of empty bins (58 percent) and a Binomial(512, 0.466) bump at 238. LOGISTIC forms a comb at multiples of its 174.8 cycle visits.

Measured D (markers) against the parameter-free prediction (dashed) from the exact one-period histogram, the REAL*4 rounding cells, or the logistic rho model, for every depth-scan series. The prediction follows every turn, including the seed-65536 swing from D = 0.14 to $1.2\times10^5$ and the REAL*4 rise to D = 31 at $B=10^8$.

Residuals (measured minus predicted D, in units of the predicted standard deviation) for all 120 depth-scan points. Open circles mark nearly deterministic histograms. Everything lies within $\pm2\sigma$ except LOGISTIC at $B=100$, which reflects the serial-correlation widening of the null shown in the seed study.

Top: dispersion index inside blocks of $10^4$ consecutive bins at $B=10^7$, $N=10^9$, for numbers stored in REAL*4. Steps occur at every power of two, as the rounding model (dashed) predicts, with MINSTD and RANDU shifted down by their period deficits. Bottom: the resulting multimodal count-of-counts, each matched by its model; the peaks correspond to bins holding 1, 2, 3 or 4 representable floats.

Left: chi-square z of the student's test ($B=10^5$, $N=10^7$) for 200 seeds per generator. RANDU and RANDM sit near the predicted $z=-4.17$ (solid tick) in almost every run; MINSTD and RAND are shifted slightly negative; the long-period generators scatter around 0. Right: at $B=100$, $N=10^4$ the logistic map's z distribution (1000 seeds) is 1.7 times wider than N(0,1), although its mean D is 0.99.

caveats: The 200-seed runs are not independent for the short-period generators. 200 x 1e7 draws cover the RANDU orbits about 1.86 times each and the MINSTD cycle 0.93 times, so the segments overlap. The naive t-test and KS p-values for RANDU, RANDM, MINSTD and RAND therefore overstate significance. The offset between observed and predicted mean z (MINSTD -0.83 vs -1.04, naive p = 0.003; RANDU sd 1.22 vs 0.98, KS p = 7e-5) is not resolved. Single-seed depth-scan residuals for these generators are all within 1.7 sd.
The hypergeometric model assumes the partial period behaves like a random subset of the population. I confirmed this only empirically at the tested depths; there is no proof for LCG segments.
The predicted sd of D uses a per-bin Gaussian approximation and ignores the weak inter-bin correlation from the fixed total. Residuals are quoted in those units.
At B = 1e8 only lambda = 10 (N = 1e9) was affordable, not lambda = 100.

The RAND one-period table was built from the identity RAND = floor((s-1)/2^9) 2^-22, verified on 2e8 draws (0 mismatches) but not over the full 2^31-2 period. The full-period RAND run was cancelled to stay within the compute budget; RANDU, RANDM, MINSTD and their REAL*4 versions were enumerated over their full verified periods.
REAL*4 R250 uses the continuous rounding model, which is only approximate for its 2^32-point input lattice. Agreement is still within 1 sd at all depths.
The LOGISTIC rho model treats tail and cycle points as independent Poisson placements. The inflated shallow-depth variance from serial correlation (finding H9) is measured, not modeled.

Planned but not run: a fixed-N, increasing-B sensitivity scan. It is covered analytically by $z \approx -(N/P)\sqrt{(B-1)/2}$ and the $N^* \approx 12P^{2/3}$ rule, which match the observed failure depths but were not tested directly.
MIDSQ was run only with seed 777, which collapses immediately. No proper 8-digit seed was tested.
Total compute was about 25 CPU minutes on a machine with load averages of 25 to 66, so the wall-clock timings in the summary files are inflated.
rnglib_issues: No coding bug found in rnglib.f90.

Refinement of the documented RAND fact: gfortran RAND() after srand(s) equals floor((x_MINSTD_state - 1)/2^9) * 2^-22 exactly (0 mismatches in 2e8 draws from seed 777). The description 'MINSTD truncated down to a multiple of 2^-22', i.e. floor(2^22 s/(2^31-1)) * 2^-22, is wrong in 390,584 of 2e8 draws (0.195 percent). Consequence: per MINSTD period each of the 2^22 RAND values is produced exactly 512 times, and the top value 1-2^-22 only 510 times.

G_MIDSQ with the project default seed 777 (not an 8-digit seed) reaches the absorbing state 0 on the second draw (777^2/10^4 = 60, 60^2/10^4 = 0), so every MIDSQ test at seed 777 tests a constant. An 8-digit seed is needed for MIDSQ to be a meaningful negative control.

G_LOGIS in double precision is eventually periodic. Seed 777: tail 14,324,259 steps, then a cycle of 5,638,349 states (bit-exact replica verified against rng_next). 6 of 30 random seeds fall into the fixed point 0 within 1.4e6 to 1.9e7 steps, after which LOGISTIC outputs 0 forever. This is not an implementation bug, but it gives LOGISTIC an effective period of about 1e7.

Minor: with rng_single = .true., the largest REAL*4 below 1 also absorbs inputs in [1-2^-25, 1) (values that round to 1.0 are mapped back), so it carries 1.5 times the weight of its neighbours. Negligible for histograms (one bin at B >= 1e7).
